Answer Key & Explanations  
Q1. B – Section 1(2): It extends to the whole of India.  
Q2. C – Section 2(ba): Defines "collective investment scheme" as any scheme or arrangement  
satisfying conditions in Section 11AA.  
Q3. C – Section 3(3): The head office of the Board shall be at Bombay.  
Q4. B – Section 4(1)(a) & (4): The Chairman is appointed by the Central Government.  
Q5. A – Section 4(1)(d): Five other members, of whom at least three shall be whole-time  
members, appointed by the Central Government.  
Q6. B – Section 6(a): The Central Government shall remove a member if he is adjudicated as  
insolvent.  
Q7. B – Section 7A: A member must disclose the interest and not participate in deliberations or  
decisions regarding that matter.  
Q8. A – Section 8(a): Proceedings are not invalid merely due to any vacancy in the Board.  
Q9. B – Section 11(1): Duty is to protect investor interests, promote development, and regulate  
the securities market.  
Q10. B – Section 11(2)(la): Allows calling from or furnishing information to specified agencies.  
Q11. B – Section 11AA(1) Proviso: Pooling of funds involving 100 crore rupees or more, not  
registered, is deemed a CIS.  
Q12. C – Section 11AA(3)(iii): A contract of insurance under the Insurance Act, 1938 is excluded  
from CIS.  
Q13. B – Section 11B: Directions can be issued in the interest of investors or orderly  
development of the market.  
Q14. C – Section 11B Explanation: Includes power to direct disgorgement of wrongful gain or  
loss averted.  
Q15. B – Section 11C(1): The Board directs the "Investigating Authority" to investigate.  
Q16. B – Section 11C(6): Punishable with imprisonment extending to one year, or fine, or both.  
Q17. A – Section 11C(8A): Authorized officer may requisition services of any police officer or  
Central Govt officer.  
Q18. B – Section 11D: Power to pass an order requiring a person to cease and desist from  
violation.  
Q19. B – Section 12(1): Stock brokers, sub-brokers, etc., must obtain a certificate of registration.  
39  
SEBI Act, 1992  
Q20. B – Section 12A(d): Prohibition on engaging in insider trading.  
Q21. C – Section 15A(a): Penalty shall not be less than one lakh rupees.  
Q22. C – Section 15A(a): Penalty extends to one lakh per day subject to a maximum of one crore  
rupees.  
Q23. B – Section 15G: Deals with Penalty for insider trading.  
Q24. C – Section 15G: Penalty not less than 10 lakhs, extending to 25 crores or 3 times profit,  
whichever is higher.  
Q25. B – Section 15HA: Penalty for fraudulent and unfair trade practices.  
Q26. B – Section 15-I(1): Officer not below the rank of a Division Chief.  
Q27. D – Section 15J: Age is not a factor; disproportionate gain, loss to investors, and repetitive  
nature are factors.  
Q28. C – Section 15JA: Penalties realized are credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.  
Q29. B – Section 15JB(1): Application for settlement of proceedings.  
Q30. B – Section 15K: Establishment of Securities Appellate Tribunals.  
Q31. C – Section 15L: Presiding Officer and two other members.  
Q32. A – Section 15M(1): Must be sitting/retired SC Judge or sitting/retired CJ of High Court (or  
HC Judge with 7 years service per amended text).  
Q33. B – Section 15N: Term of five years.  
Q34. D – Section 15N Proviso: Maximum age is 70 years.  
Q35. B – Section 15T(3): Appeal filed within forty-five days.  
Q36. D – Section 15U(1): Guided by principles of natural justice, not bound by CPC.  
Q37. C – Section 15Z: Appeal to Supreme Court within sixty days.

cannot be compounded.
